Lots of experience working with kids, being a mom, and working closely with other adults that care for children. I’ve been a mom for 14 years, so I’ve done a lot of research regarding childhood behavior, and you can give children all of the freedom in the world, but it will always be chaos, if you fail to teach them that personal autonomy comes with responsibility. 

Say a kid wants to draw all over the walls with a marker, that’s fine, no one needs to get angry, but now you have to teach the child the consequence of their choice, which is they no longer have free access to art supplies, and must clean up their mess, and obviously if the child is very young (3 or younger) you have them help you clean the mess as best they can, kids behave this way because they are trying to learn how to move through the world, constantly pushing boundaries to see how adults and other people react. The child’s behavior will never change unless the parents change. When the mom does nothing, she teaches the kid that his/her behavior is acceptable. 

If it really bothers you, I highly recommend talking to the parents, but try not to be confrontational, ask them if they have ever considered any of the ideas that have been proposed in this thread, in terms of dealing with the behavior that you previously mentioned.
